title: Task Intake and Acceptance
body:
Overview

This record belongs to the End-to-End Workflow Benchmark Database (public edition), a database that measures complete task completion rather than isolated component scores, from intake to verified deliverable. Task Intake and Acceptance covers the following: turns a plain request into a written task with acceptance criteria agreed before work starts. The record is written as a complete, usable file: it states what the entry is, how it is used, and what its limits are, and it carries a demo program that was genuinely executed at build time, with its output stored beside the code. Benchmark honesty: this database defines part of the fixed test suite for the R32 capability collection. Its target is 99% measured reliability on defined tasks (TARGET, not measured result). The comparative measurement run comes after building and is not claimed anywhere in this round.

How it works

A workflow benchmark run starts from a plain request, walks every stage in order, and counts the task complete only when the final deliverable passes its acceptance gate, including verification and failure-recovery stages. Applied to this record, the method means the following in practice: turns a plain request into a written task with acceptance criteria agreed before work starts. The record sits at ladder rank simple in the teaching ladder, which runs simple, then compounded, then most complex, so a reader can start from the simpler records and work toward this one.

Worked example

The demo walks a small workflow through its steps and prints steps completed, elapsed minutes, and completion. The demo program prints:

Workflow steps: 6
Steps completed: 6/6
Elapsed minutes: 24
Complete: True

Use and limits

A workflow score describes the tested workflow path only. A shortcut that skips verification may finish faster while failing the acceptance gate, and it is counted as incomplete, not as fast. In practice, a reader can use this record to run the same check on their own tasks: follow the method, compare the result with the worked example, and record any difference with its evidence. The record is one of sixteen in this database, and it cross-links to related databases so the reader can continue from here without guessing where to look next.

Record fields: workflow_stage: retrieval; task_class: retrieval of existing records; acceptance_gate: acceptance criteria met; sample_tasks: 100 fixed tasks.
